The provided text aligns strongly with the conventions of the hardboiled detective and noir genres. By setting the narrative during Prohibition, it utilizes a historical backdrop that is frequently associated with moral ambiguity and systemic corruption, which are central themes in noir literature. The protagonist, a "renowned detective," fits the archetype of the cynical or weary investigator common to the genre. Furthermore, the explicit mention of themes such as morality, corruption, and the pursuit of justice confirms that the story adheres to the genre-specific focus on ethical dilemmas and the flawed nature of society. There is no significant deviation from these established genre tropes; rather, the text serves as a quintessential example of noir storytelling.

The season that comes after autumn is winter.
